facts.text: The Cité de la Biotech houses more than 5,500 people and 120 life sciences companies within a 3 km radius, including the CQIB incubator and the INRS Armand-Frappier research centre.
Phase II of the Cité de la Biotech is expected to create 7,500 new jobs over the next decade, with over one billion dollars in anticipated investment.
Laval has three times more jobs in life sciences and health technologies than elsewhere in the province.
Laval ranks among the four Quebec regions with the largest industrial diversity indices, with life sciences, agribusiness and metal manufacturing among its main sectors.

overview: Laval had 438,366 residents in the 2021 Census, up 3.6% from 422,993 in 2016. Its 169,785 occupied dwellings cover 246.13 square kilometres, and the median household income in 2020 was $85,000, higher than in the wider Montreal region.

The economy is diverse, anchored by the Cité de la Biotech life sciences park, major retail and manufacturing. A local business serves suburban families with above-average incomes who often compare Laval options with Montreal ones.

byService.lead-generation: Laval lead generation should target suburban households earning a median $85,000 with French-first messaging and offers that save families time compared with crossing into Montreal.
byService.seo: Because Laval sits beside Montreal, SEO must claim Laval-specific and neighbourhood keywords such as Chomedey and Sainte-Rose so the 438,366 residents find local options first.
byService.website-development: A Laval website should be bilingual with French as the default, mobile-fast and clear about service areas across 246.13 square kilometres of suburban neighbourhoods.
byService.branding: Laval branding can project a modern, family-oriented and science-forward identity, reflecting a life sciences hub whose population grew 3.6% between 2016 and 2021.
